The announced overall conversion is 30 points per EUR, rounded to the nearest whole EUR at final payment. A randomly selected completer has earnings multiplied by 10, with an announced minimum of EUR 100 and maximum of EUR 200. Leaving or permanent exclusion forfeits payment. The earlier game history uses these definitions. Each day you and five anonymous rematched players got 100 points each. Contributions were destroyed; group total at least 300 meant retaining 100 minus own contribution, otherwise the whole group lost the remainder with that day's stated probability (.9 or .6). On round 15 the new risk was announced for the remaining days. Beliefs are your earlier reports, not other people's reports: pnb is what you thought each member ought to contribute; ee and ne are descending five-entry forecasts of others' contributions and their personal normative beliefs respectively, each forecast paid up to 5 per entry based on max(0,5-absolute error). Conditional4 lists the four contingent contributions hh/hl/lh/ll: the first letter is whether at least three of the other five contributed at least 50 (h) or below 50 (l); the second is the corresponding majority in what they said everyone ought to contribute. The applicable entry replaces your own ordinary contribution while the other five ordinary contributions are unchanged; a separate risk draw applies. It was submitted in rounds 1,5,10,14,15,19,24,28. Daily feedback was provided at the start of the following day; only feedback with subsequent submission evidence is shown here. Anonymous other contributions are an unordered multiset, and automatic entries are marked. Missing-day feedback is not asserted to have been seen. You did not see others' current PNB/EE/NE or any forecast reward during these rounds. Four daily rounds, one in each seven-round block, were randomly selected for payment. Your day-one lottery choice was one of these fair heads/tails pairs: [28,28],[36,24],[44,20],[52,16],[60,12],[70,2]; the realized outcome was not revealed until final payment. Your earlier SVO positions follow the six endpoints [[85,85,85,15],[85,100,15,50],[50,85,100,85],[50,85,100,15],[100,50,50,100],[100,85,50,85]] in the order [self_left,self_right,other_left,other_right], with screen payoffs linearly interpolated and rounded to whole points. The actual day-one questionnaire item answers are not reconstructed in this input; this does not mean you did not answer them. Predict this participant's joint contingent punishment decision after the 28 daily collective-risk rounds. You are anonymously paired with a randomly chosen other participant. Both receive 30 points. Enter how many of your own points to spend for each case of the partner's round-28 contribution: below 50, exactly 50, above 50. Each entry is independently between 0 and 10; these are alternatives, not three simultaneous expenditures, and their sum need not equal 10. If your decision is selected, spending s leaves you 30-s and reduces the partner's 30 points by 3s. The partner also submits such a strategy based on your round-28 contribution. One person's strategy is randomly implemented. The partner's actual contribution and current strategy have not been revealed. The original form's heading asks how many points to reduce; its preceding instructions and implementation use the entered value as own spending, not the threefold deduction. Output only an object with keys partner_below50, partner_equal50, partner_above50 containing the three entered spending amounts.
